In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds, and I bless and give peace to him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and to his family and his Companions and whoever is guided by his guidance and follows his way until the Day of Judgment. To proceed: God, glorified and exalted, built this world upon an everlasting struggle between truth and falsehood. The two sides of this struggle are the party of God and the party of Satan. As for the party of God, its leaders are God's infallible messengers, and its lamp is the clear revelation sent down from God, mighty and majestic. As for the party of Satan, its leader is Iblis, upon whom be God's curse. This struggle is the benefit of the earth: if it stopped for a single moment the earth would be corrupted, because God made this abode a house of works and not of recompense, and made after it the hereafter a house of recompense and not of works. As for this abode: if truth alone were in it, it would have no meaning, because people would then deserve to enter the Garden; and if falsehood alone were in it, so that truth had no voice, God's wrath and detestation would come.

"My Lord has been angry today with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before, and the like of which He will never be angry after." For that reason God instituted in it the mutual repelling of these two parties, so that this should be a benefit to the earth and a continuation of natural life upon it. God Most High said: {And were it not for God's repelling people, some of them by others, the earth would be corrupted} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:251). The benefit of the earth, then, is the existence of this everlasting struggle upon it.

The party of God, since Muhammad (peace be upon him) was sent, is represented by this Muhammadan community, the followers of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him). For everything that those before held fast to has been abrogated; and this Book sent down upon Muhammad (peace be upon him) is a guardian over all the Books, confirming the truth that is before it. What it has confirmed and endorsed is the firm truth from God, and what it has altered and abrogated there is no returning to. Hence God Most High said: {And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will not be accepted from him, and in the hereafter he will be among the losers} (Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:85). And it is soundly established from the Prophet (peace be upon him) that he said: "By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, no one of this community — no Jew and no Christian — hears of me and then does not believe in me, but that God casts him on his face into the Fire."

God took the covenant and the compact upon all the earlier communities that they should follow this Messenger when he was sent, and took the prophets' acknowledgement of that, and said: {Do you acknowledge, and take up My burden upon that?} (Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:81) — and al-iṣr is the most binding of covenants, the strongest thing anyone takes upon another — {They said: we acknowledge. He said: then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses. (81) And whoever turns away after that, those are the transgressors} (Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:81-82). And the transgressors are those who go out from obedience to God and from His ruling.

This community God has honoured with kinds of honouring, and made it the best community brought forth for people. That is why He said in the firm part of the revelation: {You are the best community brought forth for people} (Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:110). The people of exegesis have differed over what the preposition and its object attach to in His words "for people". One party of them said it attaches to "you are" — that is, you are, for people, the best community brought forth. So this community is the one that tends the interests of people and is the witness against them on the Day of Resurrection, and is God's upright ones in the earth, and is likewise the intercessors who are not refused, and is the one that keeps faith with the other communities, and is the one that holds the messengers true and does not exceed God's right concerning them. That is why the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made it a condition of faith in him that a man believe that Jesus is God's servant and His messenger and His word which He cast to Mary and a spirit from Him; for whoever bears witness to that, after bearing witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, "it has become binding" for him, as is soundly established from the Prophet (peace be upon him).

For that reason this community was the best community brought forth for people: its goodness is for all people, that is, for the whole of humanity. And this goodness appears plainly on the Day of Resurrection, when all the prophets are disputed with by their communities. There is no messenger but that he is stood up in the assembly at the highest scene, and it is said: "Did you convey God's messages?" and he says: "I did convey." And his people say: "No bearer of good tidings and no warner came to us." And it is said: "Who bears witness for you?" And he says: "Muhammad and his community." So this community is brought and bears witness for the messengers against their disputants — even Noah, whose people dispute with him and say: "No bearer of good tidings and no warner came to us," and he says: "Indeed one did." And it is said: "Who bears witness for you?" And he says: "Muhammad and his community." So Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his community are brought and bear witness that he tarried among them a thousand years less fifty, and that he called them to God, mighty and majestic, and established God's proof against them.

As for the second view of the people of exegesis about what the preposition and its object attach to in His words "for people": that what it attaches to is "brought forth" — that is, you are the best community brought forth; that is, this community was brought forth for people. What is meant by the bringing forth of the community for people is its being sent with its civilisation and its message and its religion. This entails that this religion which Muhammad (peace be upon him) brought is the best religion for people. For the earlier religions sent down from God are truth, but there is a great distance between the reward of acting by them and acting by what the Prophet (peace be upon him) brought. Hence al-Bukhari brought out in the Ṣaḥīḥ that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Your likeness and the likeness of those before you is the likeness of a man who said: who will work for me from the beginning of the day to its middle, or to the noon prayer, for a qīrāṭ? And the Jews worked. Then he said: who will work for me from noon to the afternoon for a qīrāṭ? And the Christians worked. Then he said: who will work for me from the afternoon prayer to the setting of the sun for two qīrāṭs? And this community were the people of that. So the Jews and the Christians objected, and he said: have I wronged you of anything of your right? They said: no."

So this community's right is doubled and its reward is doubled, and therefore its religion is the best of religions. The prayer of a man of this community has the reward of many times the prayers of those before; and a man of this community's sitting in the mosque between the afternoon and sunset prayers, or between the noon and afternoon prayers, has the reward of years of the work of the monks who cut themselves off for worship in the earlier communities. All this is part of God's honouring of this community.

Likewise, part of its honouring and its goodness is that God, glorified and exalted, sent down to it the best of Books and laid down for it the best of the ways of religion, and sent to it the best of messengers, and made its miracle abiding and everlasting; and He wrote for it six things that were not in the earlier communities. For the earlier communities — none of them could pray except in the place set apart for prayer, whereas for this community the earth has been made a place of prayer and a means of purification, so that whatever man is overtaken by the prayer, let him pray. Likewise, the spoils of war were made lawful for it, and had not been made lawful for anyone in the past. Likewise, it was aided by dread a month's journey ahead: the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) was aided by that, as he reported; and he reported in another hadith that this remained for his community, so that it is aided by dread. Likewise, God, glorified and exalted, would not set over it one who would uproot it at the root, so that there must remain of it those who uphold the truth, whom neither those who oppose them nor those who fail them can harm, until God's command comes while they are upon that. Likewise, the burden was lifted from it, and much was made lawful for it of what had been forbidden to the earlier communities. Hence God Most High said, addressing the People of the Book: {Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written down with them in the Torah and the Gospel, who enjoins upon them right and forbids them wrong, and makes lawful for them the good things and forbids them the foul things, and lifts from them their burden and the shackles that were upon them: those who believe in him and honour him and help him and follow the light that was sent down with him, those are the prosperous} (Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:157).

Among what God has also singled out this community with is that He made its scholars like the prophets of the Children of Israel; for the Children of Israel were governed by their prophets, and this community is never without a scholar who upholds God's proof. So its leaders are its scholars, who preserve the revelation sent down upon the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), and they are God's trustees over this revelation. God would not put His revelation in a house of dishonour, for God creates what He wills and chooses — they have no choice — and He would not entrust it to the bankrupt. Whoever is bankrupt, untrustworthy, a betrayer, God would not entrust him with His revelation; rather to God, glorified and exalted, belongs the choice and to Him belongs the dominion, and none can reverse His ruling. Therefore He chooses for the preservation of His revelation the trustworthy, who are God's trustees over His revelation and who sign on behalf of the Lord of the worlds.

Likewise, among the particular features with which God has distinguished it is that He brings forth for it, at the head of every hundred years, one who renews for it the affair of its religion; and this is what the community needs at all times. Whenever a phase of the phases has passed and one layer upon another, there comes one who renews the affair of the religion. They are a band cooperating in righteousness and God-fearing: among them are the scholars who act on their knowledge, and among them the truthful, sacrificing strivers, and among them the accomplished statesmen, and among them the seasoned economists, and among them those who uphold the command and do not fear the blame of any blamer in God's cause, and among them the soldiers who are in the right, and among them the women who keep to what God has laid down, and among them the young who prefer the hereafter to the first life. These renew the affair of the religion: whenever a layer has passed and a new layer comes, there comes forth among them one who renews for this community the affair of its religion.

But with all this, and with this great honouring, God would not leave the believers upon what they are in except after arduous examinations. This is God's way that has run its course; it is not injustice and not a breaking of a cosmic law. Rather, none of the prophets has passed, nor of the righteous who succeeded them, but that he was examined with an arduous examination upon this sound course. Hence God Most High said: In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.

{Alif Lām Mīm. (1) Do people reckon that they will be left to say "we believe" and not be tried? (2) And We tried those before them, and God will surely know those who are truthful and will surely know the liars. (3)} (Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt 29:1-3). It is soundly established from the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) that he said: "The most severely tried of people are the prophets, then the next most exemplary and the next." Here is Abraham, the intimate friend of God, whom God honoured above everyone who preceded him among people, and honoured likewise above all besides him except Muhammad (peace be upon him): {and God took Abraham as an intimate friend} (Sūrat al-Nisāʾ 4:125). With all this, God tried him and examined him with kinds of trials and tribulations. When his son reached the age of walking with him, he was commanded to slaughter him. He was examined likewise with arduous commands, that he should leave his bondwoman and his son in a valley with no cultivation, in which there is no water and no pasture, but only ravening beasts. Yet Abraham completed this examination and passed with distinction, and God bore witness to that for him, saying: {And when his Lord tried Abraham with words, and he fulfilled them} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:124). He passed the whole examination a hundred per cent, and the prize was the words of God Most High: {He said: truly I am making you a leader for people} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:124). So all people are bound to take Abraham as their example; none goes against him but one who has made a fool of himself, and none turns away from the creed of Abraham but one who is foolish and has made a fool of himself.

God commanded Muhammad (peace be upon him) to follow the creed of Abraham, and commanded you, company of believers, to follow the creed of Abraham; and He made clear this creed which ought to be followed, and it is the devoting of servitude to God alone, and complete loyalty to God and complete disavowal of God's enemies. This is the creed of Abraham which you have been commanded to follow: {There has been for you a good example in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people: truly we are quit of you and of what you worship besides God; we disbelieve in you, and between us and you there has appeared enmity and hatred for ever, until you believe in God} (Sūrat al-Mumtaḥanah 60:4) — alone. So everything Abraham did of that or said is an example for the believers which they must take as their example and follow — except one thing, namely his asking forgiveness for his father; for this one thing God excepted from the following of Abraham, and said: {except Abraham's word to his father, "I shall surely ask forgiveness for you"} (Sūrat al-Mumtaḥanah 60:4). As for what is besides that of Abraham's guidance, God has approved it for us all and commanded us to follow it.

God's trying of this community is very great, and there is repeated in it the like of what went before for the earlier communities. God has recounted to us many of the trials of the earlier communities so that this should be a steadying for us and a preparation for us, so that the matter should not take us by surprise and those who fall away should fall away. God, glorified and exalted, made clear some of His examinations of the Children of Israel, and said in the firm part of the revelation: {Have you not seen the notables of the Children of Israel after Moses, when they said to a prophet of theirs: raise up for us a king, that we may fight in the way of God?} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:246). The first examination directed to these, after their enthusiasm had been roused and they had said "raise up for us a king that we may fight in the way of God" — the first examination directed to them was: {He said: might it be that if fighting were prescribed for you, you would not fight?} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:246). In this examination they all failed, and not a single one of them passed: {They said: and why should we not fight in the way of God, when we have been driven out from our homes and our children?} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:246). So the fighting is not in the way of God after all, but for the sake of the homes and the children: {when we have been driven out from our homes and our children}.

After this theoretical examination came the practical examination, which is the performance of striving in the way of God: {and when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away, except a few of them} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:246). The practical examination is always easier than the theoretical examination: in the theoretical examination all the examinees fail, and in the practical examination a few of them pass — as will recur for you in these verses. In the first, theoretical examination no one passed. The second examination was practical: {and when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away, except a few of them} — a small group of them passed.

Then after this came another theoretical examination, namely the placing above them of one whom they did not see as deserving to be placed above them; and this examination is arduous for souls, for many souls are built upon envy, and upon seeing their own superiority over others, and upon self-admiration. That is why their prophet said to them: {Truly God has raised up for you Talut as king} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:247) — and this is an examination from God. And they all failed this examination: {They said: how can he have the kingship over us, when we are more entitled to the kingship than he, and he has not been given abundance of wealth? He said: truly God has chosen him over you and has increased him in breadth of knowledge and of body; and God gives His dominion to whom He wills, and God is all-embracing, all-knowing} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:247). God, glorified and exalted, steadied them with an extraordinary matter, namely the descent of the angels carrying an ark from heaven in which was the tranquillity and in which were the remains of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron had left. That was of God's favour, glorified and exalted, because when they failed this arduous examination it would have been hard for a party to come forth from them after that to strive in the way of God. So when the clear signs came to them and the angels came down carrying the ark from heaven, in which was a tranquillity from God and a steadfastness upon the truth, and in which was a remainder of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron had left, that entailed a passing and a rise in morale and a steadfastness upon the truth.

Then after it came another practical examination, namely His words: {And when Talut set out with the troops, he said: truly God is trying you with a river; whoever drinks of it is not of me, and whoever does not taste it is of me, except one who scoops a scoop with his hand. And they drank of it, except a few of them} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:249). Al-junūd is a plural of paucity — that is, those who remained with Talut were a small number, because their failure in the earlier examinations had already occurred; and even so, of those too only a few remained: they all drank from the river, except a few of them.

Then after this came another examination, and it is very arduous, namely the contemplation of the encounter: when these strivers remember the strength of their enemy and see that they are many times their number, and that in their hands is material power, and that the good things of the earth are put at their service against them — this is without doubt an arduous examination. That is why He said: {And when he crossed it, he and those who believed with him} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:249) — and they are few of few of few — {they said: we have no power today against Goliath and his troops} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:249). This is a theoretical examination in which they all failed. After this God steadied a small group with the truth, and they are those who reckon that they are to meet God — that is, who are certain that they are to meet God; that however long they lived, their destiny is to God: {wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you were in towers raised high} (Sūrat al-Nisāʾ 4:78). And the one death God has written is a single one:

*And whoever does not die by the sword dies by something else: the causes are many and death is one.*

This death cannot be lifted by flight and cowardice, nor can it be hastened by advancing and courage. That is why Ibn Muhammadi, may God have mercy on him, said:

*Neither does holding back bring on what we have been spared, nor does pressing forward ward off what we are to meet.*

What God, glorified and exalted, has written must come to pass. That is why He said: {How many a small band has overcome a numerous band by God's leave! And God is with the patient} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:249). These are the ones who were able to stand firm, because they had grounded themselves upon a creedal principle from which they set out, so that their creed was a driving force for them towards advancing, because they reckon that they are to meet God. God Most High bore witness for them to the truthfulness and soundness of their creed, and that is why they were the ones who endured the encounter. And with that they declared openly what their creedal motive required, and said: {How many a small band has overcome a numerous band by God's leave!} They did not merely hold it in their souls but declared it openly, so that it should increase them in steadfastness and certainty.

For this reason we need to study together such a subject as the one before us, namely the concerns of this community; we need to study it as those men said: {How many a small band has overcome a numerous band by God's leave! And God is with the patient. And when they went forth against Goliath and his troops they said…} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:249-250). They did not rely upon material power; rather they raised their hands to God: {They said: our Lord, pour out upon us patience, and make our feet firm, and help us against the disbelieving people. So they routed them by God's leave} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:250-251). He did not say "they routed them by their own powers," nor "by their courage," nor "by their machines"; rather He said: {So they routed them by God's leave, and David killed Goliath, and God gave him the kingship and wisdom and taught him of what He willed. And were it not for God's repelling people, some of them by others, the earth would be corrupted; but God is possessed of bounty towards the worlds} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:251). This is God's way that has run its course, and that is why God followed it with His words: {And were it not for God's repelling people, some of them by others, the earth would be corrupted}.

This way is always repeated, so that God examines people, because this faith is not a statement to be said or a claim to be claimed; rather it must be confirmed by action. Those who believed with the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) in Mecca met with plain hardship, which if you remembered it today your eyes would overflow with tears and there would arise in you a great deal of pity and mercy. When one of you remembers the state of those confined in the mountain pass, who were besieged for three years, forbidden to buy and sell and marry, with no one giving them any charity, and with no crops of their own and no watering, and no trade and no resource of the resources of life… Many of them recount to us something of what they suffered. Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas says: "I went out one night in the pass to relieve myself, and my hand fell upon something, and I shook it, and it was a cloak; so I divided it in two halves between myself and ʿUtbah ibn Ghazwan, and I wrapped myself in half of it and ʿUtbah ibn Ghazwan wrapped himself in half of it." And he also says: "I went out, while we were in the pass, to relieve myself, and my hand fell upon something. I brushed the dust from it, and it was a hide; so I brought it and roasted it and ate it, I and my brothers." And ʿUtbah ibn Ghazwan says: "I saw us in the pass with the Prophet (peace be upon him), and there was not one of us but he was binding a stone upon his belly from hunger. Then, by God besides whom there is no god, I saw those very men, and there was not one of them but he was a governor over one of the garrison cities."

God, glorified and exalted, was able to help His Messenger (peace be upon him) without this siege; but it was His wisdom and His way that has run its course which made the idolaters besiege the believers in the pass, so that the believers should be formed with a formation this community needs. For those men who were besieged in the pass — this world after that was not worth anything to them. Hence Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas says, as in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī: "By God, I am the first of the Arabs to shoot an arrow in the way of God; and I saw us campaigning with the Prophet (peace be upon him) with no provision but the leaves of the gum-acacia and this ḥublah plant, so that one of us would relieve himself as a ewe does, without anything mixed in it. Then the Banu Asad have come to reprove me over Islam — I should have failed indeed, then, and my striving would be lost."

If one of you thinks about that siege and is pained within himself at what the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) and his Companions met with of the plotting of the idolaters, he ought also to remember that this is part of God's plan and of His mercy to this community, and that were it not for this siege those men would not have been formed who were able to carry the banner of Islam to every place. The Meccan period, which lasted thirteen years, is the period in which the men of this community were formed and were brought up with a complete upbringing; and this upbringing yielded thirteen centuries of the life of this Islamic state. The Meccan period was thirteen years, and every year yielded a whole century of the life of this community. The community now needs the Meccan period anew, and for that reason the nations have set upon it by God's way, glorified and exalted, as a purification and a sifting, and so that He may take from among you martyrs. Then after that the remaining remnant of you remains, aided, whom neither those who oppose them nor those who fail them can harm; and it is they at whose hands God grants the opening. This sifting must be general to the community and must occur, for it is the way that has run its course.

The examinations of this community in the first age were not limited to what the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) and his Companions met with in the Meccan period; rather they continued even in the Medinan period. The Prophet (peace be upon him) made clear to them what would occur in this community of trials and calamities and afflictions. Hence in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, from the hadith of Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, may God be pleased with him, he said: "I came to the Prophet (peace be upon him) while he was reclining upon his cloak in the shade of the Kaʿbah, and I said: 'Messenger of God, will you not seek help for us? Will you not supplicate for us? Do you not see what we are in?' He said: 'Among those before you a man would be brought and a saw would be placed upon the parting of his head and he would be split in two with it; and then combs of iron would be brought and he would be combed with them beneath his bone, of skin and flesh, and that would not turn him from his religion. And by Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, God will surely complete this affair, until a rider travels from Sanʿaʾ to Hadramawt fearing none but God, and the wolf for his sheep. But you are a people who are in haste.'" This was not to happen in those times, which are the times of upbringing and formation. These are God's ways that have run their course: one who is at primary level cannot be prepared for a doctoral thesis, and one who is at intermediate level cannot be fit for the university level, and so on. This is God's way in upbringing.

For that reason the believers, after they emigrated to Medina, also witnessed various kinds of these trials and concerns. Among the most extreme of them is the examination that occurred on the day of Uhud, when the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) went out after the people had pressed him to go out, which he had not seen fit. For he was of the view that the idolaters should be fought from the strongholds, so that whoever of them came would be killed and they would turn back defeated without the Muslims falling into exposure to danger. But the young men, the people of enthusiasm, forced him to put on the armour of war and to prepare for striving. So when he went in to wash in order to put on his armour, he put it on and went out. "They said to him: 'It is as though we have pressed you, Messenger of God.' He said: 'Indeed.' They said: 'We repent to God, so do what you saw fit.' He said: 'It is not for a prophet, when he has put on the armour of war, to take it off until God judges between him and his enemies.'"

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) went out and his crier called among the people. At that time the rabidness of the hypocrites in Medina increased, so that one of them, blind of eye and blind of insight, set about throwing dust at the army and saying to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him): "Had I known that the dust would reach your face, I would have turned it towards you." These hypocrites, when the time of fear comes, their thorn grows sharp against the Muslims; and when the fear goes, they melt away as though they had never been and had never had any effect at all. So the hypocrites banded together, and a party of them went out with the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) to discourage whomever they could of the army.

When the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) had passed the houses and gone out from the dwellings of the Banu Umayyah ibn al-Harith of the Khazraj, he set up his camp short of Uhud, and he raised the banner of the Emigrants and the Helpers, and under it gathered seven hundred of those who reckon that they are to meet God, of the truthful. And ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul raised the banner of hypocrisy, and under it gathered the like of that number of the hypocrites; and he went back with half the army, away from the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), after he had seen the idolaters advancing in their pride and their enmity to Islam. So ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr ibn Haram, the father of Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, went forward to them and stood over them and said: "My people, do not fail the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) in this situation, when you have seen the battle line." They said: "If we knew there would be fighting, we would follow you." And they returned to their dwellings, and God, mighty and majestic, exposed them.

The examination here was not merely the return of half the army; rather the examination was more arduous than that, when defeat crept into the souls and the people were routed away from the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), and only ten men and one woman stood firm with him, while he stood in the face of the enemy saying, "To me! To me!" fighting in the way of his Lord. This examination was very arduous, and yet forgiveness came after it. Hence God Most High said: {Truly those of you who turned away on the day the two hosts met — Satan only made them slip because of some of what they had earned; and God has pardoned them} (Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:155).

After it came another arduous examination, namely the examination of the Confederates, when the Ḥums came with all the means of power they possessed, and the ten tribes of Ghatafan came with them, and the Qaysis came with them, and the bedouin who were around Medina came with them wanting plunder and spoil, and the Banu al-Nadir came with them, and the Banu Qurayzah broke the covenant. So there came about the state which God Most High described at the time of hardship in His words: {O you who believe, remember God's favour upon you when hosts came against you, and We sent against them a wind and hosts you did not see; and God is seeing of what you do. (9) When they came at you from above you and from below you, and when the eyes swerved and the hearts reached the throats, and you thought various thoughts about God. (10) There the believers were tried and shaken with a severe shaking. (11) And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a sickness said: God and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion. (12) And when a party of them said: people of Yathrib, there is no standing for you, so turn back. And a group of them asked leave of the Prophet, saying: truly our houses are exposed — though they were not exposed; they wanted nothing but to flee. (13) And had it been entered upon them from its sides and then they had been asked for apostasy, they would have given it, and would not have delayed over it but a little. (14) And they had already covenanted with God before that they would not turn their backs; and the covenant of God is a thing to be answered for. (15) Say: flight will not profit you if you flee from death or slaying, and then you would not be given enjoyment except a little. (16) Say: who is it that will protect you from God if He intends evil for you or intends mercy for you? And they will not find for themselves, besides God, any ally or helper. (17) God knows those of you who hinder and those who say to their brothers "come to us," and who do not come to the fighting except a little. (18)} (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:9-18).

In this state which came about, people's stances diverged into four stances. The first stance is the honourable stance which God recorded as a testimony in the firm part of His revelation for the Emigrants and the Helpers, for the truthful of this community, for the righteous example whom the later generations of the community ought to follow: {And when the believers saw the Confederates they said: this is what God and His Messenger promised us, and God and His Messenger spoke truly; and it increased them only in faith and submission. (22) Among the believers are men who have been true to what they covenanted with God: some of them have fulfilled their vow and some of them are waiting, and they have not changed in the least. (23) That God may reward the truthful for their truthfulness and punish the hypocrites if He wills, or turn to them in forgiveness} (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:22-24).

This honourable stance is what required of these men faith and submission: faith in the executing decree and submission to the Law as well. They are the ones who combined the decree and the Law. In the matter of the decree they believed in what God decreed and knew that what God has written must come to pass and that the means avail nothing against it — the pens have been lifted and the pages have dried. And with that, in the matter of the Law, they put to work the means they were capable of, knowing that they are charged with performing them. So they could not rely only upon the prior decree, nor depend upon what has been written; rather they had to put the Law to work and to strive and to expend what they were able. That is why Nusaybah fought with two swords, and Talhah ibn ʿUbayd Allah shot on the day of Uhud until his hand was paralysed, and Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas shot before the Prophet (peace be upon him) while the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said to him: "Shoot — may my father and my mother be your ransom" — and he never joined his two parents in a ransom for anyone else.

This great and honourable stance which these men took is repeated whenever the campaign of the Confederates comes again. Whenever this examination comes, we find those who increase in faith in God's decree and increase in submission to God's Law: they believe that what God has written must come to pass, and they are submissive to God's ruling — they must be led and must carry out what God and His Messenger (peace be upon him) have commanded.

The second stance is the stance of the open hypocrites, who were waiting for their moment; and this moment came at the time of weakness, so they declared openly what they concealed: {And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a sickness said: God and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion} (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:12). They say: Muhammad promises you that the treasures of Chosroes and Caesar will be opened to you, and here you are today, not one of you able to go out to relieve himself. Yes indeed — the treasures of Chosroes and Caesar were opened and were spent in the way of God, and we are among those who bear witness to that; and God and His Messenger spoke truly, and those who set up equals to God lied. This open stance is repeated also, as we shall see.

Then the third stance is the stance of the people of favour-currying among the hypocrites and the sick of heart who try to discourage. They are unable to declare openly the defeatism they find in themselves, but they discourage people from helping God and His Messenger: {And when a party of them said: people of Yathrib, there is no standing for you, so turn back} (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:13). There is no difference between the two readings: lā muqāma lakum, that is, there is no settled place for you here — they want defeat from them; and lā maqāma lakum, that is, there is no use in you and no benefit in your standing and your coming, so turn back, that is, be routed. These are the hinderers, the discouragers, who say to people: what are you doing? And whom are you fighting? And what do you want? Your enemies — no one can stand in their way. And these discouragers likewise have their stance repeated, as you will see, whenever the campaign of the Confederates comes.

The fourth stance is the stance of the weak in mind and management among the believers, who withdrew upon their own private interests and abandoned the affair of the community, and said: come, let us set right our farms and the walls of our houses. These are the ones whose stance God recorded in His words: {And a group of them asked leave of the Prophet, saying: truly our houses are exposed} (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:13) — ʿawrah, that is, not inside the wall — {though they were not exposed; they wanted nothing but to flee}. So God, mighty and majestic, named the turning back to private interests a flight from the battle and a retreat from the helping of God and His Messenger. God, mighty and majestic, made clear that these men held fast only to the weakest and slightest of hairs, and that is why He said: {And had it been entered upon them} — that is, their houses — {from its sides} — that is, from its edges — {and then they had been asked for apostasy, they would have given it, and would not have delayed over it but a little} (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:14) — that is, they would have given it to whoever asked them for it; and in the other reading la-atawhā, that is, they would have fallen into it. We ask God for safety and well-being. And al-fitnah here is apostasy from Islam. So these men who withdrew upon their private interests, had they known that they would not be secure over their property and their houses and their families unless they declared apostasy from Islam, they would have done it. And this is what we also witness whenever the campaign of the Confederates is repeated.

Today we are witnessing a new campaign, which is the campaign of the Confederates; and it is one concern among the concerns of this community — but it is the prominent concern which many of you thought of when you heard this title, "the concerns of the community." There is no doubt that many of you are thinking of two concerns:

*People have one concern, and I today have two concerns: the loss of the privy and the loss of Shaykh ʿUthman*

— as Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, said. You are thinking of two concerns: a concern in Palestine and a concern in Afghanistan. But the reality is that the concerns of the community are more and greater than that. These two concerns we cannot be indifferent to, nor diminish their importance; but we shall apply to them what God has accustomed us to in the campaign of the Confederates, and you will see the results, God willing.

First: the banding together of the hypocrites and the idolaters and the Confederates against this community is nothing new; rather it is what is familiar, and had they not done it they would have been reckoned traitors. Had the Jews' enmity to the Muslims not grown severe, the Jews would have betrayed their principles and gone back on their own affair. And had America not invaded the Muslims in the heart of their own home, America would have declared bankruptcy and retreat — for they have no principle from which they can set out in their lives except enmity to this religion and plotting against its people. This principle is what is hidden from many people.

For many people, when some injury befalls God's enemies, whatever that injury may be, say: this is an assault upon the innocent. What does "the innocent" mean? The innocent, as you all know, are the non-criminal — is that not so? This is the basic definition of the innocent: the non-criminal. Do you know a crime greater than associating partners with God and denying His messengers? How can one who has disbelieved in God and denied God's messengers, upon them be blessing and peace, be described as innocent? No one has ever committed a crime greater than this crime. For that reason, one who has disbelieved in God and denied His messengers can never be described as innocent — and especially when we know that these disbelievers are plundering the good things of the Muslims and altering their religion and raiding it at all their hours.

Their permanent war against this religion is not confined to the military side, as one who is not aware of the state of people imagines. The war in the creedal field, and in the intellectual field, and in the field of morals and values, and in the field of learning, and in the economic field, is a standing war of long duration. One of the makers of American policy declared before us at an international Islamic conference in Riyadh — he declared before the audience, with a number of ministers and princes and doctors and university professors present, he declared from an Islamic platform — that they plunder only 85% of the good things of our land and give us 15% in charity. A witness from their own people bore witness to that: 85% of the good things of our lands they plunder, and they give us charity and want thanks from us for 15% of the good things of our lands which God has given us. Then after this, there is no doubt that they wage war with every means they possess upon the very foundation of our belief. The doubts that Muslim youth in the lands of Islam fall into, and what occurs when crises come of the showing of hypocrisy and the retreat from God's religion and the abandoning of commitment to it — all of it is from these people's plotting and the effects of their work, and of their permanent, continuing campaigns which seek to Christianise people and seek likewise to corrupt their morals and seek to spread kinds of vice among them. All these campaigns are continuing, and none denies them but one heedless or feigning heedlessness.

The war standing today against Islam — whether that be in Palestine, or in Afghanistan, or in Chechnya, or in other places among the lands — has its counterpart in another war which many people do not feel, from which no house of stone and no house of clay in the whole world escapes: it invades you here in the heart of your own home. This war — search for it and you will find it in your own breasts. There is not one of you but he has been invaded in his breast, in his convictions, until he denies his own reason and is convinced of something reason does not endorse. Many of you believe the claims that the Western media spread and are convinced by them and see them as certainties not open to dispute and discussion. And if one of you wanted to convince his mother or his maternal aunt of the falsity of what the London radio or Monte Carlo had announced, she could not believe him. Why? Because the invasion has entered into the innermost core of hearts. They have invaded you with this educational invasion established in the schools and the curricula, and with this media invasion from which no house is free.

That is why you hear things which the least intelligent of people would find objectionable. If you asked the least intelligent of people: is it possible for a small group of prisoners, shackled hand and foot, in a fortified castle, surrounded by soldiers on every side, to rise up from their castle and fight for four days — fighting aircraft and tanks and missiles and kinds of deadly weapons for four days — and then for a group of them to be victorious and escape? This is something no one could believe. And yet all people believe it, because it came in the Western broadcasts. It is what you heard about the affair of Qunduz: that about twenty thousand of the Afghans and those with them of the Arab Afghans and others were besieged in it, and that they were taken prisoner and put in the castle, and that they took the weapons from their guards, and that they fought for three days, and a group of them escaped, and that they killed a large number of American and English officers. It has today become one of the fixed certainties with many people that it is a play just as the Westerners wove it and as they staged and spun it. The reality is that no sane man believes this. Prisoners shackled hand and foot, who are in a fortified castle on a mountain top, guarded by guards from outside the castle — how do they fight for four days and then a group of them is victorious and escapes? This cannot be believed. But because there is no Islamic media, and the news cannot reach you as it is, you have come to cling to what is said, so that you believe something you take up with your tongues and say with your mouths what you have no knowledge of.

Taking up with the tongues is a dangerous matter, for the instrument of taking up is the ear, not the tongue; and a man takes up with his tongue only when he says a thing without thinking about it. The affair of the slander (al-ifk) was taken up by people with their tongues without passing through their ears and without reaching their hearts; for had it passed through the ears, they would have conveyed it with full trust to the hearts, and then they would have thought about it and known its falsity. But they took it up with their tongues directly and spoke of it without its passing through their ears and without thinking about it. So it is today in every question of this kind of slander and calumny which the Western media spread: people cling to it and take it up with their tongues, so that people hear it and believe it without thinking about it.

The affair of this incident does not much concern us; but since we have mentioned the falsity of the Western claim about it, we must touch upon something of the truth in it. The city of Qunduz did indeed have in it a large number of Afghans and those with them of Arabs and Pakistanis and others, and they were besieged from two roads leading to the city, and those who besieged them were of the forces of the Northern Alliance. When the siege grew severe upon them, they had previously wanted to leave the city and hand it over to certain tribes; and the American aircraft bombarded them with every kind of bombardment, as is customary. But on the day they decided to withdraw, they called for those who wished to break their fast in the Garden — and this is their custom, to ask those present: which of you wants to break his fast today in the Garden? So a group of young men, not exceeding three hundred and seventy men, made themselves ready, and they said: we will protect the rear. And they set out with God's blessing, and they withdrew, and no encounter took place. And those three hundred and seventy remained.

They dealt with one of the Tajik commanders and gave him money to secure their rear for their departure, and he stipulated a heavy sum from them; and after they had given it to him and had gone out, they sensed treachery and that he would betray them from behind them, and that he had informed the Shiʿi Wahdat party about them and had set an ambush for them on the road. So they took counsel about what to do, and finally decided not to fight the Tajiks whom they had left behind them, because they were of Rabbani's forces, and not to go to the Shiʿah ahead of them, because they did not know their military size. So they decided to attack the American forces stationed in the city of Mazar-i-Sharif; and they did indeed attack them and found them off guard, and killed a large number of them, more than seven hundred, and killed some of their senior commanders. And indeed the aircraft bombarded them, so that most of them were killed and some of them escaped. This is the story which the Western media wove in the first form which you heard and of which you were all made certain, and which you accepted without reviewing it in yourselves.

This story is not the only one that has happened; rather its like has been repeated many times in Afghanistan and in Palestine and elsewhere. The equation is simple: the idolaters see that the utmost punishment with which they can punish people is killing and bombardment and the demolition of houses; and the striving Muslims see that the greatest medal and the greatest honour is martyrdom in the way of God. So then, what do they want from them?

One who looks at the level of the Western media and listens supposes that a shameful defeat has befallen the Muslims, and that what befell them was something they could have done without, and that it should not have been undertaken at all, and that it is among the reckless ventures with no benefit behind them. But the reality is that the war was already standing, and that the idolaters had decided to invade Afghanistan and other Islamic countries at the end of the year two thousand and one. They decided that in the year two thousand and announced it, as a witness from among them bore witness — the Pakistani minister of defence, who reported that they had informed him that the war would be upon the Taliban in Afghanistan at the end of the year two thousand and one. So the plan was ready a year in advance, and the aircraft carriers had been crouching for months in the Arabian Sea and in the Gulf and elsewhere.

Likewise, part of this media war is that many of you hear that a Palestinian blew himself up in a public place or in a Jewish military barracks in the Holy Land, and that the Jews thereupon carried out combing operations and closed the Palestinian cities and burned the olive trees and the farms, and killed enormous numbers of Palestinians and demolished houses and launched raids upon the cities with aircraft and missiles. And so one says: this Palestinian could have done without blowing himself up. The reason is that you have heard this media analysis whose implication is this. But the reality is otherwise. What made the Palestinian blow himself up? What brought the Jews to defile the Holy Land? What are they doing to the Muslims in the prisons? What are they altering of God's sanctities and of the holy places in which there is not one of the earlier prophets but that he worshipped God in them? The cause is passed over by the media and not touched upon; rather it goes to a nearby matter and builds a judgment upon it.

The Americans, for instance, claim that the cause of their invasion of Afghanistan is the explosions of the eleventh of September which occurred in New York and Washington, and claim that Usamah bin Ladin was behind them, and that the Taliban were behind Usamah bin Ladin — and the behind-ness goes on in a chain: behind the Taliban also are all the Muslims, and behind the Muslims is Islam itself, and behind that are God's hosts which they cannot number. The reality is that Usamah bin Ladin is one man among the Muslims, and among the Muslims are a billion men and more, and they are all eager to enter the Garden and all afraid of the Fire, and all of them ready to please God and His Messenger and ready to sacrifice for the religion which the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) brought, and all of them ready to strive in the way of God. If Usamah bin Ladin were killed or captured — one better than he has been killed and captured; and God said in the firm part of His Book: {And Muhammad is only a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. If then he died or were killed, would you turn back on your heels? And whoever turns back on his heels will not harm God in the least; and God will reward the thankful. (144) And it is not for a soul to die except by God's leave, a decree with an appointed term. And whoever desires the reward of this world, We give him of it; and whoever desires the reward of the hereafter, We give him of it; and We shall reward the thankful} (Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:144-145).

The Jews, upon them be God's curses, said before that the problem of Palestine is Shaykh ʿIzz al-Din al-Qassam — an aged man; but they feared him, because they supposed that all the terror came out from under his turban. So ʿIzz al-Din al-Qassam was killed. What happened after that? Did striving in the way of God in Palestine stop? Then they supposed that Ahmad Yasin was behind the intifada, and Ahmad Yasin was imprisoned, and he is now under house arrest, unable to move any of his limbs except the prayer-beads with which he bears witness that there is no god but God, and except his tongue with which he terrifies the Jews. They claimed that behind the bombings was Yahya Ayyash, may God have mercy on him; and Yahya Ayyash was killed — did the bombings stop? Then they claimed that behind them was Fathi Shaqaqi, and Fathi Shaqaqi was killed — did the bombings stop? Then they claimed that behind them was Abu Hunud, and Abu Hunud was killed — did the bombings stop?

The matter continues: the fathers will die in the war, and the sons, until the grandsons fight. So long as the Muslim lands are colonised, so long as the Jews wreak havoc in the Muslims' holy places, the killing must continue. God has written upon them abasement and wretchedness, and has undertaken to them in the firm part of the revelation that He will set over them those who will visit upon them an evil punishment until the Day of Resurrection: {And when your Lord proclaimed that He would surely raise up against them, until the Day of Resurrection, those who would visit upon them an evil punishment. Truly your Lord is swift in retribution, and truly He is forgiving, merciful} (Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:167).

Nor is this particular to the Jews, upon them be God's curses, alone; rather God, glorified and exalted, set out the place of terrifying and said: {And prepare against them what you are able of force and of tethered horses, terrifying thereby God's enemy and your enemy, and others besides them whom you do not know — God knows them} (Sūrat al-Anfāl 8:60). There are others besides them whom many people do not know; and many of them are of those who profess Islam and pronounce the testimony — indeed one may pray with the Muslims in the mosque, and have been born of two upright Muslim parents, and yet he is of the others besides them whom you do not know: God knows them. Upon those God has written terror, and they shall be terrified, and the calamities shall be set upon them: {And those who disbelieve will not cease to be struck by a calamity for what they have wrought, or it will alight near their home, until God's promise comes. Truly God does not break the appointment} (Sūrat al-Raʿd 13:31). Those men do not cease to be exposed to a lash of God's punishment, either directly from God or by our hands; and we and they are waiting: {So wait; truly we are waiting with you} (Sūrat al-Tawbah 9:52).

There is no doubt that we believe that God's promise is not broken, and that God will fulfil for us what He has promised us of victory and establishment: {God has promised those of you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors in the earth as He made those before them successors, and will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them, and will surely change them, after their fear, to security. They worship Me, associating nothing with Me. And whoever disbelieves after that, those are the transgressors} (Sūrat al-Nūr 24:55).

These concerns relating to Palestine and Afghanistan and others are a small part of the concerns of this community. Many people's concern is to get the news in its correct form, and I see no ground for that; for one who searches for the news and has no share in the matter may be representing the state of the hypocrites and taking a stance of their stances. For they are the ones who wish they were among the bedouin, {asking about your news; and had they been among you they would not have fought except a little} (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:20). So do not be among the bedouin, asking about the news of the striving or about the news of this community. And know that this community is one body: if a limb of it complains, the rest of the body rallies to it with fever and sleeplessness; and that every severing that befalls any of its extremities must be felt by the other extremities, who must rise up for it.

The Jews wanted — as they reported — that America should be purely theirs, to the exclusion of the believers, and they strove for that. For after the events of the eleventh of September occurred — and we know that America possesses a great fleet of satellites, more than thirty-nine spy satellites, and possesses networks around the world for espionage, and they have mentioned that they have forty thousand employees in the Arab lands who are not known to be employed for the American security service — with all that they did not produce any proof whatever that the Muslims had any hand in the affair of the explosions: no photograph, no audio recording, no fingerprint, no signed cheque, no credit-card withdrawal, no telephone conversation, no recording in the black box of any of the aircraft. Therefore it is known that America only wants to fasten a false charge upon the Muslims, and that it is a crusading war, and that it is the other campaign of the Confederates in this age.

For that reason, observe how the stances are repeated. We have seen a great number of those who used to profess Islam and lay claim to it, whose names are Islamic names and who are of the children of the Muslims, repeat the speech of their predecessors among the hypocrites and say: {God and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion} (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:12). These have divided into two sorts.

The first sort are the people of open declaration, who want everything called striving (jihād) to be changed and that to be abolished from the religion, and the curricula of education to be changed: these curricula which produce the like of Usamah bin Ladin and the like of the Taliban must be changed, and this book which urges the fighting of the disbelievers and the idolaters must be changed. These responded immediately to a documentary film broadcast on the Western channels on Tuesday the eleventh of September, which I saw on a French channel. This film brought out about fifty clips from fifty countries of the Islamic lands, each clip representing Islam in their view. Among the strangest of what I saw in it was a clip representing a very old man from Senegal in a tumbledown hut teaching the children the Qur'an, with the writing-boards in their hands and a small whip in his hand with which he strikes them over the recitation of the Qur'an; and on one of the boards was written, while the shaykh recites, {Fight those who do not believe in God nor in the Last Day, and do not forbid what God and His Messenger have forbidden, and do not follow the religion of truth, from among those who were given the Book} (Sūrat al-Tawbah 9:29). And the commentator says: this man beats the children so that they will fight us. This is a clip representing Islam in Senegal. Another clip from Pakistan: a Pakistani woman teaching her daughters the Arabic and Urdu letters — for the Arabic letters are the Urdu letters — and she writes: alif: I bear witness that there is no god but God; bāʾ: in the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate; jīm: jihād. They say: even this woman teaches her daughters striving.

These clips which they brought out in this documentary film about Islam had their effect upon these hypocrites, so that they declared their hypocrisy openly and began to demand the changing of the curricula, and began likewise to demand the closing of the mosques and the laying down of laws to regulate them — claiming thereby that they want to preserve them and serve them — and began to demand the nationalisation of all the religious institutions, and that they should become subject to the regime, the regime being punished for their offence and held to account for what they do. And this is something that can never happen until the Messiah son of Mary comes down as a just judge, God willing.

The second sort of them are those who have been defeated with a great defeat, so that they set about denying the charging of Islam with terrorism, saying: Islam is innocent of terrorism; and they deny any connection between Islam and striving in the way of God, and in so doing they are being obstinate with an obstinacy greater than any we have known. Whoever denies striving in Islam — his denial of heaven and earth is a lighter thing than his denial of striving; for this religion is a religion of striving, and the Prophet (peace be upon him) was sent with the sword before the Hour, as he reported. These defeated men suppose that if they deny Islam's connection with terrorism, that will preserve the Muslims' main body and be the course of wisdom, and will keep matters running in their proper channels, and that they are thereby guarding against the enemies' plotting and doing it only as a precaution against them. But the reality is that this is a declaration of defeat; and these men, had they been asked for apostasy, would have given it and would not have delayed over it but a little.

The third stance is the stance of the discouragers, and how many they are in this age, in this campaign, the contemporary campaign of the Confederates. For many of them say: woe to you! Do you want to strive against America? Do you not know that America is the one in whose hand the whole affair lies and to whom the whole affair returns? They make a god of it besides God. And these forget that the White House, which is the source of decision in America, had an aircraft brought down inside it by a reckless American without the American detection systems detecting it; and they forget likewise that the most important American documents were stolen from the Department of State, and that many of the documents relating to the Iraq war were stolen from the Pentagon, and that the aircraft that struck the Pentagon — the Pentagon was informed about it eighteen minutes beforehand, and was informed that it was heading towards it, and even so it could not act within eighteen minutes: its pillars were paralysed and its limbs were sealed and it could not take any action at all. And this is nothing of God's seizing; for God, glorified and exalted, is the All-Powerful. How able He is to command the sea to swallow what is in it, and the land to swallow what is in it, and outer space to swallow what is in it, and the air to swallow what is in it! God's power has not diminished in anything.

The last stance is the stance of the defeated among the Muslims, who have turned to their private interests and abandoned the affair of the community, and have come to deny any connection with any committed person and with any striving, and say: we have no connection with those people, and there is no relationship at all between us and them. In this they are lying and are giving themselves the lie; they only wanted by that to say: {our houses are exposed — though they were not exposed; they wanted nothing but to flee} (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:13).

These four stances, now that they have become plainly evident to your eyes, we must set them all before ourselves. Each one of us must review himself while he is witnessing the campaign of the Confederates and has been present at it: where is he? Was he of the people of the first, honourable stance, who said: {this is what God and His Messenger promised us} (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:22)? For remember that the Messenger (peace be upon him) reported these trials that come before the Hour, and reported that among them are trials like patches of a dark night, in which a man rises in the morning a believer and comes to evening a disbeliever, and comes to evening a believer and rises in the morning a disbeliever, selling his religion for a portion of this world. He made clear in them (peace be upon him) the banding together of the enemies against this community, and that they will call one another to it as eaters call one another to their dish, and that this is not from fewness of number. And he made clear likewise that enfeeblement would creep into the souls of this community; and it was said: "And what is the enfeeblement, Messenger of God?" He said: "Love of this world and hatred of death." And he made clear likewise (peace be upon him) that there would be set over this community rulers who would fail this community and would not uphold the truth for God and would be with the enemies against this community.

So we all say: {this is what God and His Messenger promised us, and God and His Messenger spoke truly} (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:22). We bear witness that what the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said of that has come about and that we have seen it, so we have believed in it and held it true. But after this we must submit to God's ruling; for it is not enough that we believe in the decree without acting by the Law, for these are two addresses from God's command which must both be put into effect together. Our faith in the decree requires of us that we fear none but God, and that we know that the death God has written for us we shall die: {Every soul shall taste death, and you will be paid your wages in full only on the Day of Resurrection. So whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to the Garden has won; and the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion} (Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:185); {wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you were in towers raised high} (Sūrat al-Nisāʾ 4:78). And we know that death is only in the hand of the angel of death, whom God sends to take the soul of him whose soul He wills to take, and that that can neither be advanced nor delayed: {Our messengers take him, and they do not fall short} (Sūrat al-Anʿām 6:61). And we know that America and others of God's enemies possess neither for themselves nor for anyone else life or death or resurrection: {and if the fly should snatch something from them, they could not rescue it from it. Weak is the seeker and the sought! (73) They have not esteemed God with the esteem due to Him} (Sūrat al-Ḥajj 22:73-74).

This stance requires of us that we act, and that we hasten to the help of God and His Messenger. And here the questions of the young multiply: what is to be done? And where do we begin? And what is our striving? And is it fitting that the youth of the community should set out and cross the borders, if they are not seized at the borders, and pass over into another state for it to put them in its prisons — and then, if they escape from those prisons, go to the prisons of another state? Is this the solution?

The answer: this is not a solution, nor is it the striving required of you. Rather you must know that you have been invaded in the heart of your own home, and that the media are an invasion, and that the intellectual invasion is greater than the military invasion; and that you must hold fast to the might which God has written for you. For God has written might for His believing friends: {God has written: I shall surely overcome, I and My messengers. Truly God is strong, mighty} (Sūrat al-Mujādalah 58:21); {and God will surely help those who help Him. Truly God is strong, mighty} (Sūrat al-Ḥajj 22:40); {O you who believe, if you help God He will help you and make your feet firm} (Sūrat Muḥammad 47:7). So yours is the might God has written for you: {and to God belongs the might, and to His Messenger and to the believers} (Sūrat al-Munāfiqūn 63:8); and God has written abasement and wretchedness and humiliation upon your enemies.

But you must review yourselves and know that the victory God has promised you is conditional. So fulfil this victory, and know that leaping and burning through the stages and skipping the rungs of the ladder is not possible: a man must travel with a steady pace. For offensive striving is the summit of the hump of faith. A great number of the children of the Muslims of various nationalities have come to me who were falling short in the prayer, and every one of them says: I want to strive in the way of God. And I say: my brother — or my son — striving is at the summit and you are in the hollow; so you must first attend to the prayer, and when you have perfected it, then think about striving. One who cannot endure the prostration in the prayer cannot endure the bombardment of aircraft and missiles. Reviewing one's faith and building souls at rest and truthful with God is more important and more fitting than that we should thrust ourselves into Afghanistan or into Palestine or into Chechnya, or that we should travel and be prevented from reaching them.

For that reason we must remember the Islamic plan, without travelling by which the work of this community cannot succeed. This plan passes through seven stages. The first stage of it is the building of the Muslim individual — meaning that each individual among us should be in accordance with the good pleasure of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), in faith and assent and compliance and avoidance and formation and upbringing and readiness. When this has come about for a great number of us, then comes the second stage, which is the stage of building the Muslim family in the case of each one of us; for each one of us must try to build a Muslim family, since many of the rulings of the Law are not particular to the individual in his own private self but relate to dealings within the family and must be applied. So it is a stage prior to the stage of striving. Then when a number of Muslim families have arisen who realise the good pleasure of God and His Messenger, there comes the third stage, which is the establishing of the Muslim society which realises the rights of neighbourhood and the rights of the Muslim upon the Muslim and the right of brotherhood and truthfulness and sincerity and the absence of deceit, and realises all the social values of Islam. Then after that comes the fourth stage, which is the building of the Muslim group which watches over the interests of the Muslims and puts them before its own private interests and sacrifices for them what is precious and dear, and steps forward to receive the bullets, unfastening the buttons of the shirt and saying: {and I hastened to You, my Lord, that You might be pleased} (Sūrat Ṭā Hā 20:84). Then after this comes the fifth stage, which is the building of the Muslim state which establishes God's Law over God's servants in any patch of the patches of this wide and spacious earth, and establishes rule in accordance with what the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) and his Rightly Guided successors established. And when that is realised, there comes the sixth stage, which is the establishing of the Islamic caliphate which gathers all the Islamic states and is the symbol of their unity, and which is able to declare striving against God's enemies. Then comes the seventh stage, which is the declaring of striving against whoever has opposed God and His Messenger; and it is the teacherhood of the world. Striving is declared at that point only by one who has been able to have a state from which to declare it, and who has an army; for the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) did not declare striving against the idolaters in the Meccan period but declared it in the Medinan period, after a state had been established for him.

So the Muslims' striving is first by the establishing of an army of Muslims in whom the qualities of establishment are realised: {those who, if We establish them in the earth, perform the prayer and give the zakat and enjoin right and forbid wrong; and to God belongs the outcome of affairs} (Sūrat al-Ḥajj 22:41). Then after that the building of families in accordance with the good pleasure of God and His Messenger; then after that the establishing of the sound Muslim society which applies what God has commanded, and it is the school of striving; then after that the establishing of the rightly guided Muslim group which stands in for the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) in raising God's word high and establishing the state of Islam; then after that the establishing of the state of Islam; then after it the establishing of the caliphate; then the declaring of striving against God's enemies.

These stages must be subject to a systematic strategic planning built upon the basis of the means and the intermediate objectives, which none can undertake but the people of binding and loosing among the Muslims — and they are those who combine three qualities, namely knowledge, uprightness and soundness of judgment. Malik, may God have mercy on him, said: "I do not see them combined today in one man; and if they are not combined, then a scrupulous man of sense — for by sense he asks and by scrupulousness he restrains himself" — and in another transmission, "he keeps himself chaste."

Then this required striving does not include within it the striving against those who occupy the lands of Islam. For the Palestinians, it is obligatory upon them to strive even before the establishing of the families and before the establishing of the Islamic state; and the Afghans likewise: so long as America occupies their land it is obligatory upon them to strive, and it is obligatory upon the Muslims to help them and to assist them, all of them; and it is obligatory upon you all to take part in that. And likewise every country of the lands of Islam which the enemies of Islam have occupied and invaded — it is obligatory upon its people immediately to strive and to fight, and it is obligatory upon the Muslims to support them and help them with all the kinds of help they are able. And if they do not do so, they are the sinners; and God has no need of them nor of their help. God will help His friends, and the truth will be realised, by the might of one mighty or by the abasement of one abased; and the outcome belongs to the God-fearing. God, glorified and exalted, must raise the banner of striving, and God, glorified and exalted, must help this religion, and must subdue the disbelievers and the deniers — and that will be soon, God willing, glorified and exalted. And God is the granter of success. God is greater, and praise belongs to God; and may God bless and grant peace to our Prophet Muhammad and to his family and all his Companions.

flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW (house rule 12) — THE HIGHEST-RISK RECORD IN THIS SLICE, AND IT SHOULD NOT SHIP WITHOUT A DECISION BY UMMAH COLLECTIVE AND THE SHEIKH'S OFFICE. The second half is a political address delivered in the months after the invasion of Afghanistan, and it contains, among other things: an argument that no non-Muslim can properly be called 'innocent', since unbelief is the greatest crime, offered in answer to the objection that attacks harm innocents; a statement that armed striving is an immediate individual obligation upon Palestinians and Afghans and that it is obligatory upon the audience to take part in it; a denial that any evidence was produced tying Muslims to the attacks of 11 September, with the invasion described as a crusading war; an approving account of an attack on American forces at Mazar-i-Sharif, with a casualty figure (more than seven hundred, plus senior commanders) that no other source supports; an account of fighters volunteering to 'break their fast in the Garden'; a defence of Palestinian bombings as a response rather than a cause, with named figures (ʿIzz al-Din al-Qassam, Ahmad Yasin, Yahya Ayyash, Fathi Shaqaqi, Abu Hunud) treated as martyrs; the repeated formula 'the Jews, upon them be God's curses'; a claim that the Jews sought to have America to themselves; the seven-stage programme ending in a caliphate that declares striving and in 'the teacherhood of the world'; and sharp censure of Muslim rulers and of Muslims who deny Islam's connection with striving. Everything is translated at full strength, with nothing softened, nothing strengthened, nothing omitted and no disclaimer added by the translator, as house rule 12 requires. The record also contains a counterweight the editor should see: the Sheikh explicitly tells young men who want to cross borders to fight that this is not their required striving, that their invasion is a media and intellectual one, and that one who cannot endure the prostration in prayer cannot endure bombardment.

translator_notes: Qur'anic renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic text of the Qur'an.

A single public lecture on the concerns of the Muslim community. The Sheikh opens with the doctrine of the permanent struggle between the party of God and the party of Satan, sets out the honours and distinguishing features of this community, and then argues at length from the trials of the Children of Israel under Talut, from the boycott in the mountain pass at Mecca, from Uhud and from the campaign of the Confederates, that trial is the settled way of God. He then maps the four stances taken at the Confederates — the honourable, the openly hypocritical, the discouraging, and the withdrawal into private interest — onto the situation of the Muslim world after the invasion of Afghanistan, and closes with a seven-stage programme running from the formation of the individual to the declaration of striving.

The lecture was delivered in the winter of 2001-2002, not on the date the CMS serves; see the date flag. Every reference in it — Qunduz, the Taliban, Ahmad Yasin under house arrest, the killing of Abu Hunud — belongs to that period, and the English keeps the present tense the Sheikh uses rather than recasting it as past.

The source abbreviates the blessing upon the Prophet throughout as (ص). The English renders it in full as '(peace be upon him)' at every occurrence, which is the house convention in this corpus; the abbreviation is preserved unchanged in body_ar. The word jihād and its verb are rendered as 'striving' throughout, with the Arabic given at first mention, since the Sheikh himself distinguishes several senses of it in this lecture — the striving he declines to sanction for his young audience, the media and intellectual invasion he calls them to resist, and the defensive obligation he affirms for the occupied. Collapsing all of these into a single English word would obliterate a distinction he makes at length.
dec: Argues that no non-Muslim can properly be called innocent, that armed striving is an immediate individual obligation, and gives an approving account of an attack on US forces.
